summary: Compiled the five M5-S04 outputs from sources already on disk: configuration-workbook.md (104 rows across the ten canonical sections plus Other configuration, collated from workbook/*.md, with all 103 pending:M5-S03 source_story_id cells resolved against artefacts/M5-S03/story-backlog.md's own RTM and the three CWB-OTHER-001..003 backslash-pipe source_req_id cells re-delimited with ';' as workbook/99-other-configuration.md's own note anticipated); traceability.md (58 requirement rows copied verbatim from the build's traceability.md Matrix, plus a coverage line: 0 requirements with no step, 4 steps with no requirement row (M3-S05, M5-S02 blocked; M5-S03/M5-S04 documentation steps), 24 of 26 manual tests outstanding); deploy-order.md (build-wide ten-slot sequence assembled from every workbook row's own 'Deploy position' citation, 103 of 104 rows accounted for); acceptance-criteria.md (67 Given/When/Then records collated from the M5 story backlog's 11 stories, plus 39 more from every `manual` acceptance test the plan declares on a step or milestone, to give uat-test-cases.yaml something to resolve `ac_id` against); and uat-test-cases.yaml (39 cases, one per plan-declared manual test, given/when/then text taken verbatim from each test's own description). Four declared checkers were run verbatim: check_rtm.py exits 0 (4 pre-existing WARNs); check_workbook.py, check_ac_format.py and check_uat_case.py all exit 1 on genuine, pre-existing or newly-surfaced gaps named in full below — none papered over by inventing content this run has no source for.
confidence_rationale: check-outputs exits 0 (every declared output present, non-empty, parseable) and the coverage line reports no requirement without a step, which is the HIGH bar per Step 11 — but three of the four declared acceptance checkers exit 1 on real gaps this compile run surfaced rather than caused (missing automation-selection.md decision-tree citations on every Section 6 row; nine/three rule-type requirements with no negative UAT criterion; a fourth instance of the checker's un-escaped-pipe parsing defect in CWB-AUT-029), which caps this run at MEDIUM rather than HIGH.

process_observations.observation: check-outputs exits 0 on all five declared outputs and check_rtm.py exits 0 on the compiled traceability.md, confirming the per-step rows this build wrote all the way back to M1-S01 collate cleanly into one build-wide document without a single orphan or missing-requirement gap.

check_workbook.py fails 30 of 30 Section 6 (Automation) rows for missing an `automation-selection.md Q<n>` citation, even though plan.json declares `decision_trees: ["standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md"]` on M3-S04, M3-S05, M4-S03 and M4-S05 — the citation was never written into the workbook row's notes cell at any of those four steps' own documentation runs, so this is a pre-existing gap across four steps' worth of rows, not something this compile run introduced or can safely invent (the specific Q-branch that resolved each choice is not recorded anywhere this run may read).

CWB-AUT-029's target_value cell quotes a naming-pattern regex containing two backslash-escaped pipes (`BeforeSave\|AfterSave\|...`) — check_workbook.py's parser splits on every literal `|` with no escape handling, so this one row's columns shift under check_workbook.py exactly as workbook/99-other-configuration.md already documented for CWB-OTHER-001..003, but this occurrence was not previously named anywhere. Left verbatim rather than rewritten, because the pipe is a regex alternation operator here, not a multi-value delimiter — converting it to ';' would change what the regex means, unlike the CWB-OTHER-001..003 fix.

check_ac_format.py and check_uat_case.py both fail on rule-type requirements (assignment/auto-response/escalation rule, entitlement process) whose only UAT-phase criteria are the happy-path ones the M5 story backlog and the plan's own manual tests carry — REQ-005, REQ-023, REQ-033, REQ-034, REQ-036, REQ-037, REQ-040, REQ-041, REQ-053 (acceptance-criteria.md) and REQ-013, REQ-025, REQ-038, REQ-040, REQ-043, REQ-053 (uat-test-cases.yaml) carry no criterion or case marked negative. This is a genuine sandbox-UAT coverage gap the compile run surfaces rather than invents: the corresponding fall-through/deny behaviour for these requirements was proven only at the metadata-checker level during the build (e.g. M3-S04's own acceptance tests), never restated as a UAT-phase negative case.

Six of the story backlog's 43 raw criteria (US-CASE-002 AC-3/AC-4, US-CASE-003 AC-4, US-CASE-009 AC-3/AC-4, US-CASE-011 AC-3) carry no req_id in story-backlog.md's own Requirements Traceability Matrix. They are reproduced in acceptance-criteria.md's narrative section for completeness but were not given a lintable YAML row, because minting a req_id for them would be this run deciding a linkage the story backlog itself never made — a human should confirm whether that's an oversight in the backlog or a deliberate omission.

39 build-wide manual-test AC/UAT records had no req_id anywhere in traceability.md for five steps or milestones (M3-S05, M5-S02, M5-S03, M5-S04, M5-S05, plus three M5 milestone-level tests). Each was assigned the closest-fit already-existing req_id with the reasoning recorded in the compiled documents (e.g. M5-S02 -> REQ-058, whose own text is literally about the sandbox-owner gap M5-S02 is blocked on) rather than a fabricated id — a human should confirm these five approximations are acceptable rather than assuming they are load-bearing links.
